todo_line: - [ ] 006 Add and focused-test the signed-in read-only targeted-add route with same-club person/group resolution, current display authority, sign-in return, protected-detail denial, heading focus, selected-person and already-member states, and scanner-safe GET behaviour that performs no membership mutation.
outcome: An authorised signed-in group participant or club admin can open `/groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id` and see that active same-club person in a focused Members-page targeted-add panel, or a clear already-member state, while every GET remains read-only and unauthorised or invalid targets disclose no protected person details.
scope: Route `GET /groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id` through the existing `:club_member` LiveView session to `MemberDashboardLive` with a distinct action that selects the Members section and preserves both opaque route identities across initial mount and live navigation.

Load the ordinary dashboard/group surface first, then permit targeted presentation only when the current actor has the existing current authority to add custom-group members: current authoritative participation in that custom group or current club member-management authority. An ordinary group outsider must not receive the targeted person state.

Resolve the route's person and group together through `Membership.resolve_custom_group_target_authoritatively/3` using the host-selected club ID. Use only its server-owned person, membership, group, and `active_group_member?` facts for the targeted panel; collapse invalid, missing, built-in, cross-club, inactive-person, mismatched-group, and unauthorised cases into existing generic forbidden/not-found handling without rendering the target name or membership identity.

Present a single targeted person within the existing Members page. For an active person outside the group, show the approved `Add to <group>` panel, person name/initials, club-member context, and explanatory admission/welcome copy. For a person already in the group, show the approved accessible `already a member` status and their existing member row without an actionable Add control.

Focus the targeted panel heading on arrival using the project's existing LiveView `JS.focus` pattern and a focusable heading/stable DOM IDs. Keep the ordinary member list and permitted group metadata visible beneath the panel, including the outside-admin privacy boundary that withholds conversations.

Add focused route, request, and LiveView tests covering routing and sign-in return, participant and outside-admin access, ordinary-outsider denial, invalid/cross-club/inactive targets without protected disclosure, selected-person and already-member rendering, focus markup, and scanner-safe GET/mount behavior that creates no group membership and sends no welcome.
scope_exclusions: Do not dispatch `Membership.add_custom_group_member/2`, add the target, send a welcome, or wire a functioning targeted Add event in this packet. Confirmation-time actor/target rechecks, idempotent mutation, and welcome behavior belong to task 007.
Do not implement targeted Cancel or Escape handling, return-focus to ordinary Add member, success announcements, or post-add member-row focus; those interaction transitions remain task 007.

Do not change the accepted Membership resolver contract, the existing admission command/aggregate rules, request-access message/UI behavior, email rendering, or general custom-group picker/removal behavior.

Do not expose a target through projected club-member candidate lists before the authoritative target resolution and actor-display authorization succeed. Do not reveal target names, IDs, membership state, group member rows, or conversation data in a denial response.

Do not permit built-in group targeting, cross-club host/route combinations, inactive targets, inactive actors, arbitrary query/body identities, or authority derived from the emailed URL. The URL identifies a candidate only.
Do not implement or enable the iteration-066 browser journey, edit acceptance feature files, or remove its `@todo`; browser plumbing remains task 008.

Do not edit the approved plan, ADRs, iteration acceptance criteria, or project reference docs. Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, or another unscoped full-suite command in this packet.

references.facts: The targeted path belongs beside the existing dashboard group routes in the browser plus club-member-required pipeline; this preserves host-selected club context, authentication, and sign-in return behavior.

The existing routed LiveView coordinates selected group state, resets transient picker/request state in `handle_params/3`, and delegates protected surface loading to `MemberDashboardPresentation`. Add route-specific target state without allowing it to leak when navigating to another group or ordinary Members route.

Current authoritative group participation plus current member-management permission produce `can_add_custom_group_members?`; ordinary outsiders receive no private members, while outside admins receive Members-only data. Reuse this established actor-display boundary before assigning a targeted person.

The accepted public resolver casts all three typed IDs, reads the Club aggregate for active membership identity, custom same-club group ownership, and current participation, then returns a narrow person display summary. It already rejects invalid/missing/cross-club/built-in/inactive targets and remains the target source of truth.

The targeted state must remain the existing Members-page surface, not a separate approval screen. Place its focused panel before the ordinary picker/guidance/list and preserve the outside-admin lack of a Conversations tab.

Reuse the picker/person visual language, stable IDs, design tokens, and existing `phx-mounted={JS.focus()}` pattern. Avoid a new LiveComponent; a stateless targeted presentation component is sufficient if extraction improves clarity.

Unauthenticated club-host GETs already store the full safe club URL before redirecting to `/auth`; add a focused regression proving the new target path survives that flow rather than introducing new auth mechanics.

Accepted focused coverage proves server-owned facts, current already-member/non-member state despite stale group projections, and rejection of malformed, missing, cross-club, built-in, and departed targets. Route tests should prove safe mapping and disclosure behavior, not duplicate the resolver's internals.

Existing admission tests establish that participants and outside club admins can manage a custom group, ordinary outsiders cannot, stale projected group participation grants no controls, and GET-driven member management uses the existing Members page. Keep task-006 route tests in a focused sibling file if that keeps cases isolated.
Extend the focused route contract with both route parameters and the new LiveView action under `[:browser, :club_member_required]`.

The approved target scene shows `Add to Board`, one identified active club member, admission/welcome consequences, current members underneath, and an already-member status with no Add action. The link itself changes nothing.
Opening the signed-in authorised target page is read-only, scanners are safe, narrow layouts retain person/action readability, and arrival focus lands on the targeted heading.
The selected person is meaningful, refreshable LiveView state and therefore belongs in the route and `handle_params/3`, not client-only DOM state.
Active club membership and Admin authority remain Club-owned facts; the read route confers no write authority and must align with current membership rules.
Current group participation, not stale preference or projected UI state, governs participant access; an absent ordinary member receives no private group surface.
Keep the LiveView as route/screen coordinator, use stateless presentation components and stable semantic IDs, and keep authorization decisions out of HEEx.
Use route-driven `handle_params/3`, `JS.focus`, and selector-based LiveView tests against stable IDs rather than raw HTML.

constraints: The host-selected club remains the club authority. Never derive club context from the person ID, group projection, query params, email body, or referer.

Resolve actor surface authorization before assigning target details, and resolve the target through `Membership.resolve_custom_group_target_authoritatively/3`; do not query Ecto person/membership/group schemas directly from the LiveView.

Treat the targeted URL as identity only. A participant or outside club admin may see the target panel under existing rules; an ordinary outsider, inactive actor, or actor lacking current authority gets existing generic denial behavior.

The route is GET/read-only on both disconnected render and connected LiveView mount. It must not dispatch any membership command, emit a group-membership event, send a welcome email, create pending state, or alter conversation/follow access.

Use the resolver's `active_group_member?` value for the already-member decision so stale projections cannot offer a target already admitted or hide a target just removed from the group while still active in the club.

Do not rely on the broad projected candidate collection to validate the routed person. It may be used only for ordinary picker behavior after route authorization and authoritative target resolution are complete.
Use stable IDs for the targeted panel, heading, person row, status, and future action seam. The heading must be programmatically focusable and receive `JS.focus` on arrival without inline JavaScript.

Preserve existing group privacy: an outside admin may manage Members but still sees no Conversations tab/content; denial responses must not contain the target name, membership ID, member list, group email, message subject/body, or compose controls.
Keep targeted presentation responsive and aligned with the existing picker/member-row classes and design tokens. Do not add a new component system or inline script.
Do not use `Process.sleep/1`; synchronize through LiveView rendering, strong command helpers, projection barriers, or `_ = :sys.get_state/1` where necessary.
completion_evidence_required: Return every changed path and identify the new route/action, route-param lifecycle, actor authorization boundary, and exact call to `Membership.resolve_custom_group_target_authoritatively/3`.

Show participant and outside-admin target pages rendering only the server-resolved active same-club person, with the Members section selected, stable targeted IDs, focusable/focused heading markup, and outside-admin conversation privacy preserved.
Show the already-member state uses authoritative current participation, renders no targeted Add control, and leaves the existing member row visible.

Show malformed/missing IDs, cross-club person/group combinations, built-in groups, inactive targets, ordinary outsiders, and actors without current display authority receive generic denial/not-found behavior whose response omits protected target details.
Show an unauthenticated club-host GET redirects to sign-in and stores the complete targeted URL for return.
Show direct HTTP GET plus connected LiveView mount perform no membership mutation, emit no group-add event or welcome email, and leave an outside target outside the group.
Confirm no targeted admission event, welcome dispatch, Cancel/Escape behavior, success status, post-add focus, acceptance-feature change, or browser-journey enablement was included.
Record each focused validation command, working directory, exit status, and test/failure counts; list any unresolved issue.

latest_review.summary: Task 005 was accepted with all focused LiveView, selected domain, and existing admission-browser checks passing; it left no review gap or unresolved candidate origin.

latest_worker_result.summary: The accepted predecessor added only the fixed Request access placeholder interaction and its two authorised assertion migrations. It did not add the targeted route, person presentation, explicit admission, or iteration-066 browser journey.
